The seagull's wings and body repeatedly distort, smear, and shrink unnaturally during flight and approach.
The seagull's body collapses, drastically shifts size, and wings deform into incoherent patches while descending toward the water.
The seagull abruptly smothers and melts into an amorphous shape as it touches the water before reforming.
